claims: --quota-floor can overshoot when Arkham doesn't send a Remaining header — tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:543-546, :1058, check at :1000; quota.remaining only updates from the X-Intel-Datapoints-Remaining header or the intel-usage poll every 500 addresses, so the run can use up the reserve the floor protects
When Arkham sends Usage and Limit but not Remaining, the headers are recorded but remaining is never derived from limit − usage, so the commit's claimed fix only works at 500-address intervals
If the start poll fails (:583, :601) and no headers arrive, remaining stays null and the floor never fires; the only sign is a warning
The intel-usage fallback overwrites the usage/limit values taken from the headers (:596-597)
A bad flag can turn into an unlimited run — tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:116, :125-126, :107-110; `--limit --no-refresh` or `--limit` with no value falls back to Infinity, so the whole ~68k queue runs
`--limit=100` is silently ignored, because only an exact `--limit` match is recognised
Unknown flags are accepted without complaint; with --chain now optional, a typo like `--dryrun` starts a paid live run

tier2 still drops its own tags when merging into an existing label — tier2-light-forensic.mjs:672-679; it builds [...existingEntry.tags, ...derived.tags] and keeps only the first 20, so tier2's forensic tags are not written for 20-tag tier1 labels
A source that hits the page cap only prints a warning — tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:284-287; it should be added to failedSources and the cap should be recorded in the inventory JSON

Addresses that errored are never retried on resume — tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:809-815; {address, error} progress lines count as done, so the 10-errors-in-a-row stop (:954-968) message that the progress file 'resumes the queue' is wrong and those addresses are skipped for good
Outdated comment — run.sh:44 still says 'A dry run touches neither Arkham nor Upstash', contradicting the rewritten header
Existing issue: progress lines are written before the batched Upstash writes, so a crash mid-batch marks up to 99 paid results as done that were never written

judge_reasoning.3845594538: The review only notes that a crash mid-batch leaves progress lines marking unwritten results as done, and calls this pre-existing. It never identifies splice-before-pipeline dropping the batch on a transient Upstash error, or that the circuit breaker misses it.
judge_reasoning.3845596185: Finding 4 says a source hitting the page cap only warns, and should be added to failedSources as incomplete discovery.
judge_reasoning.3845603922: Not mentioned. The review's run.sh notes cover printf -v, exports and a stale comment, not the tfvars key prefix match.
judge_reasoning.3845603940: Not mentioned. The review says the sanitizeEntry copies match the shared helper and raises no concern about slicing before dedup.
judge_reasoning.3845607361: Finding 3 identifies the tier2 merge building [...existingEntry.tags, ...derived.tags] and slicing to 20, which drops forensic tags when tier1 labels already hold 20 populatedTags.
judge_reasoning.3845618202: Not identified. The review holds up mergeRefreshEntry's ordering as correct and never flags that a tier1 refresh puts fresh Arkham tags first and truncates away tier2 ctp:/type: tags.

1.why: noteQuotaHeaders (:533-550) only sets quota.remaining from the Remaining header. The body fallback runs only at start and every INTEL_USAGE_EVERY=500 addresses (:1058), so between polls the :1000 check sees a stale value and can run up to ~500 lookups past the default floor of 50.

2.why: When only Usage and Limit arrive, :541-542 store them and never compute limit−usage, and remainingFromHeaders stays false. So remaining only changes when the 500-address body poll runs, even though the commit message says partial headers are fixed.

3.why: logIntelUsage catches the error and only warns (:583/:601). The start call at :859 doesn't abort, so with no headers remaining stays null and the :1000 floor check does nothing until a later poll succeeds. The run fails open.

4.why: True that :596-597 overwrite usage and limit while remaining isn't from headers. But those fields are only read by quotaLine() for logging, so nothing functional breaks.

5.why: flagValue returns undefined for a missing value or one starting with '--' (:116), and numericFlag then returns the Infinity fallback (:125-126). So `--limit --no-refresh` bypasses the 'hard parse failure' fix, and :855 applies no cap.

6.why: flagValue uses args.indexOf(name), an exact match, so `--limit=100` is never found. It silently falls back to Infinity with no error, which means an uncapped paid run.

7.why: No argv validation exists anywhere. --chain now defaults to 'all' (:134), and both the script's dryRun check (:108) and run.sh:47-48 match `--dry-run` exactly, so `--dryrun` starts a live Arkham run.

8.why: tier2:672-679 puts existingEntry.tags before derived.tags and slices to 20. This is the known 'Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels' item.

9.why: At :284-287 a HARD_PAGE_CAP hit only adds a log suffix and isn't added to failedSources. Already covered by the known page-cap items (:311/:328).

10.why: Error lines {address,error} are written before noteFailure (:1025-1040), and resume adds any line with an address to processed (:809-812). So addresses that tripped the new circuit breaker are skipped for good, even though its message (:966) says the progress file resumes the queue.

11.why: run.sh:44 (added in this diff) says a dry run touches neither Arkham nor Upstash. The rewritten header at :15-18 says the dry run does read Upstash and mint a token.

12.why: Progress is appended at :1007 before the batched flush (:1009), which is the same root cause as the known 'failed flush discards the batch and marks the addresses as processed' defect.
